lines.japanese: 四時間目は体育でした。
lines.english: Fourth period was gym.

lines.japanese: 運動能力全般に恵まれない私には辛い時間ですが、それだけに終わったあとの感慨もひとしおです。
lines.english: A difficult hour for someone not blessed with athletic ability of any kind. All the more reason to appreciate its ending.

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃん、次どうする？」
lines.english: “Tama, what should we do next?”

lines.japanese: 「午後イチ？　どうするって何、英語でしょ」
lines.english: “First thing in the afternoon? What do you mean? English, right?”

lines.japanese: 「違うよう、四時間目の次っていったらお昼ごはんに決まってるでしょー。学生さんにとっては、一日のうちでいちばん重要なイベントだよ？」
lines.english: “Nooo, after fourth period obviously means lunch. It's the most important event in a student's day, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……分からないでもないけど……」
lines.english: “Well... I can see that, I suppose...”

lines.japanese: 「なに食べる？」
lines.english: “What are you having?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、悪い。きょう私、食べないかも」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. I might not eat today.”

lines.japanese: 「かも？」
lines.english: “Might?”

lines.japanese: 「ん、じゃあ食べない。動きすぎちゃって、ちょっと胃がそんな状態じゃない」
lines.english: “Okay, then, I won't. I moved around too much. My stomach's not really up to it.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、午後死ぬよー？」
lines.english: “Whaaat? You'll die this afternoon.”

lines.japanese: 「平気だよ、一食ぐらい」
lines.english: “I'll be fine. It's one meal.”

lines.japanese: 「死ぬってー。私ならぜったい死ぬもん、タマちゃんも死ぬよう。死ぬ死ぬ、間違いなく死ぬよ」
lines.english: “You will. I'd definitely die, so you will too. You'll die, die, absolutely die.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな何度も殺さないでよ……」
lines.english: “Don't kill me so many times...”

lines.japanese: タマちゃんにふられて、ひとり寂しく学生食堂に向かいました。
lines.english: Turned down by Tama, I headed forlornly to the cafeteria alone.

lines.japanese: うちの学食は厳粛な封建主義がまかり通っているので、ほとんどの席は、三年生や有力な部活動のひとたちが占拠しています。
lines.english: Strict feudalism prevails in our cafeteria, so most seats are occupied by third-years or members of powerful clubs.

lines.japanese: だから普段の私はここでタマちゃんとお弁当を買って、教室で机をくっつけて食べるのが常でした。
lines.english: Normally, Tama and I buy boxed lunches here, then push our desks together and eat in the classroom.

lines.japanese: でもひとりでお弁当を広げるのはちょっと感傷的な気分になってしまうので、きょうは軽くサンドイッチでも買って、のんびり歩きながら食べることにしようと思います。
lines.english: But spreading out a boxed lunch alone would make me a little melancholy. Today, I'll just buy a sandwich and eat while walking leisurely around.

lines.japanese: 「はっ！」
lines.english: “Ah!”

lines.japanese: 学食のパン売り場で、私はみたび彼女に遭遇しました。
lines.english: At the cafeteria's bread counter, I encountered her for the third time.

lines.japanese: そうです。プリンセスです。
lines.english: Yes. The Princess.

lines.japanese: パンを求めて静かに列をなす学生たちの中で、彼女はむやみに声の大きい三年生の男子と連れだっていました。
lines.english: Among the students quietly lining up for bread, she was with a pointlessly loud third-year boy.

lines.japanese: 「なになに、おまえ何してんの。何してんのじゃねーか。パン買うんだよなそりゃ、ぎゃはは」
lines.english: “What's up, what's up? What're you doing? Wait, that's stupid. Buying bread, obviously. Gahaha!”

lines.japanese: お、おまえ呼ばわりです。たいへんです。どうやら三年生男子の口ぶりから推測するに、渡来さんとは浅からぬ仲のようです。
lines.english: H-he's addressing her so familiarly. This is serious. Judging by the third-year's tone, he and Watarai seem to be more than casual acquaintances.

lines.japanese: なんてことでしょう。あのふしだらプリンセスと来たら、羽田先輩というひとがありながら、これはまるで俗にいう──
lines.english: What can this mean? That shameless Princess has Haneda, yet this is just what people call—

lines.japanese: ──浮気？
lines.english: —cheating?

lines.japanese: 「え！　え？　ええっ！」
lines.english: “Huh?! Huh? Whaaat?!”

lines.japanese: とんでもない場面を目撃してしまいました。ど、どど、どうしよう、警察に……違うよ、家庭裁判所……でもなくて、えっとえっと、羽田先輩に？
lines.english: I've witnessed something terrible. Wh-wh-wh-what do I do? The police... No, family court... Not that either. Um, um, Haneda?

lines.japanese: 言えないよ！
lines.english: I can't tell him!

lines.japanese: そんな、だって、信じていたひとに裏切られてたなんて知ったら、きっと先輩は大いに悲しまれるでしょう。
lines.english: Because if he learned he'd been betrayed by someone he trusted, he would surely be terribly sad.

lines.japanese: そして人間に絶望し、世界に背を向け、孤独の海に溺れてしまうかもしれません。
lines.english: He might despair of humanity, turn his back on the world, and drown in a sea of loneliness.

lines.japanese: しかし、そんなとき現れたひとりの後輩。彼女の献身的な優しさは傷心の彼を温かく包み、そして新たな愛がそこに──
lines.english: But then a younger girl appears. Her devoted kindness warmly enfolds his wounded heart, and there, a new love—
“—That's it!”

lines.japanese: ようし、そうと分かればさっそく密告しちゃいましょう。ほうら丁度よいところに、羽田先輩もパンの列に並んでいるじゃありませんか。
lines.english: Right. Now that I know, I'll go tell on her immediately. Look, how convenient. Haneda himself is in the bread line.

lines.japanese: って、えええ！？　いたんですか！
lines.english: Wait, whaaat?! He was there?!

lines.japanese: どどど、どうしましょう、プリンセスが愛人と逢引きしているそのわずか五人前に、まさしく羽田先輩ご本人がいらっしゃったですよ！
lines.english: Wh-wh-what do I do? Haneda himself is only five people ahead of where the Princess is meeting her other man!

lines.japanese: お体がカウンターの方を向いてますからまだ気付いてはおられないようですが、あの愛人さんの声量を考えれば発覚するのも時間の問題──
lines.english: He's facing the counter, so he doesn't seem to have noticed yet. But with the other man's volume, it's only a matter of time—

lines.japanese: 「ああっ！」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: ──愛人の手がプリンセスの肩に！
lines.english: —the other man's hand is on the Princess's shoulder!

lines.japanese: 「あわわわわ……」
lines.english: “Oh, oh, oh...”

lines.japanese: たたた、たいへんです。衝撃のスクープ映像です。私は心のシャッターをばしゃばしゃ切りながらも、しかしどうか羽田先輩が気付きませんようにと祈って──
lines.english: Th-th-this is serious. Shocking footage, an exclusive scoop. Clicking my mental shutter again and again, I pray that Haneda won't notice—

lines.japanese: 「わーっ！」
lines.english: “Aaaah!”

lines.japanese: ──羽田先輩、振りむいちゃったあああ！
lines.english: —Haneda turned around!

lines.japanese: 動転した私は背中を向けて駆けだしました。
lines.english: In a panic, I turned my back and ran.

lines.japanese: 教室に戻ってから思ったこと。私はなぜ逃げたのでしょう。
lines.english: After returning to the classroom, I wondered. Why had I run away?

lines.japanese: 「あ、リンダおかえり」
lines.english: “Oh, welcome back, Linda.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ねータマちゃん、なんで私すぐ逃げちゃうのかなあ」
lines.english: “Oh, hey, Tama. Why do I keep running away?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、私に聞かれても」
lines.english: “Why are you asking me?”

lines.japanese: 「でも聞いて。あのね、いま私、現代社会の性の乱れを垣間見てきちゃったの」
lines.english: “But listen. Um, I've just glimpsed the loose sexual morals of modern society.”

lines.japanese: 「……今度はなに。学食でいちゃついてるカップルでも見た？」
lines.english: “...What now? Did you see a couple flirting in the cafeteria?”

lines.japanese: 「いちゃついて……はいなかったかなあ」
lines.english: “Flirting... Maybe not.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ何してたの」
lines.english: “Then what were they doing?”

lines.japanese: 「男の方が女をオマエって呼んで、あと肩掴んでた」
lines.english: “The man addressed the woman very familiarly, and grabbed her shoulder.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ。で？」
lines.english: “Huh. And?”

lines.japanese: 「でじゃないよ、社会問題だよ。現代日本の倫理感では大奥もハレムも認められてないんだよ」
lines.english: “Not ‘and.’ It’s a social problem. By modern Japanese moral standards, you can’t have a shogun’s harem, or any other kind!”

lines.japanese: 「……あのさ。リンダの話は、いつも要点を行間に詰めすぎだと思う」
lines.english: “...You know, Linda, I think you always pack too many of the important details between the lines.”

lines.japanese: 「今回はだいじょぶ。決定的瞬間をいっぱい脳裏のフィルムに焼きつけてきてやったもん。へへん、これがもう動かぬ証拠だねっ」
lines.english: “This time it'll be fine. I burned lots of decisive moments into the film in my head. Heh. That's undeniable evidence!”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、現像できれば？」
lines.english: “Well, if you can develop it?”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃん、紙とペン！」
lines.english: “Tama, paper and a pen!”

lines.japanese: 「机に入ってるんじゃない？　知らないけど、ここリンダの席だし」
lines.english: “Aren't they in your desk? I don't know, but this is your seat.”

lines.japanese: 「任せて、美術５の画力でいま真実を白日のもとに晒しちゃうよ。ピュ、ピュー、ピューなんとか賞も獲得しちゃうよ」
lines.english: “Leave it to me. With the drawing skills that got me a five in art, I’ll expose the truth in broad daylight. I’ll even win the Pu, Pu, Pul-something Prize.”

lines.japanese: 「ピューリッツァー賞」
lines.english: “Pulitzer Prize.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、何それー、イタリア料理みたい」
lines.english: “Ha ha, what's that? Sounds like an Italian dish.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ！　そういえば私なにも食べてない！」
lines.english: “Ah! Come to think of it, I haven't eaten anything!”

lines.japanese: 「もう一回、学食行ってくれば？　午後死ぬらしいよ」
lines.english: “Why not go back to the cafeteria? Apparently, you'll die this afternoon.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、死ぬ死ぬ。ぜったい死ぬ。タマちゃんも死んじゃうから一緒に行こうよ」
lines.english: “Yes, die, die. Definitely die. You'll die too, Tama, so come with me.”

lines.japanese: 「だから私は……」
lines.english: “I told you, I'm...”

lines.japanese: 「……ま、いっか。そこまで誘ってくれる友達は大事にしよう」
lines.english: “...Well, all right. I should appreciate a friend who wants me along that badly.”

lines.japanese: 「わあい、タマちゃーん！」
lines.english: “Yay, Tama!”

lines.japanese: 「わっ、やあらかい！」
lines.english: “Whoa, so soft!”

lines.japanese: 「捏ねない捏ねない」
lines.english: “No kneading.”

lines.japanese: というわけで学食に戻ってきました。
lines.english: And so we returned to the cafeteria.

lines.japanese: こんどはタマちゃんもいっしょです。
lines.english: Tama was with me this time.

lines.japanese: 昼休みが残り十数分で終わり、という時間帯なので、私たちは珍しくテーブル席に着くことができました。
lines.english: With only ten-odd minutes left before lunch break ended, we were unusually able to get seats at a table.

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 私がさっきパン売り場で目撃したことを（渡来さんの名前は出さずに）話しますと、タマちゃんは食べおわった菓子パンの袋をくしゃりと握りつぶしました。
lines.english: As I explained what I'd seen at the bread counter, without using Watarai's name, Tama crumpled the wrapper of the sweet bread she'd finished eating.

lines.japanese: 「リンダはいいね、好きなひとがいて」
lines.english: “You're lucky, Linda. Having someone you like.”

lines.japanese: 「ちっとも良くないー」
lines.english: “Not lucky at all.”

lines.japanese: 「もー、ちゃんと聞いてたー？　恋なんてね、しないで済むならしない方がいいの。つまんないことで馬鹿みたいにおろおろしちゃって、そいでいて良いことなんて滅多にないんだもん」
lines.english: “Honestly, were you listening? If you can avoid falling in love, it's better not to. You get all flustered like an idiot over stupid little things, and hardly anything good happens.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、朝のリンダはすっごく幸せそうだったよー？」
lines.english: “But you looked really happy this morning.”

lines.japanese: 「あーうん、しゃーわせだったー」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. I was sooo happy.”

lines.japanese: 「でしょ。それが羨ましいって言ってるの」
lines.english: “See? That's what I said I envy.”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃんも恋をしなよ。恋はいいよー」
lines.english: “You should fall in love too, Tama. Love is wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 「切り換え早いね……」
lines.english: “Quick change...”

lines.japanese: 「うん。恋する乙女は支離滅裂で情緒不安定だから」
lines.english: “Yes. A maiden in love is incoherent and emotionally unstable.”

lines.japanese: 「みたいだね」
lines.english: “Seems like it.”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃんが恋愛すれば、小説のネタにもなって一石二鳥なのに」
lines.english: “If you fell in love, you'd get ideas for your novels too. Two birds with one stone.”

lines.japanese: 「それはちょっと思うけど、でも相手いないんだもん、仕方ないでしょ」
lines.english: “I've thought that a little, but there's nobody. Can't help it, can I?”

lines.japanese: 「えー！　タマちゃん、もてるんだから、いつだって始められるのにー」
lines.english: “Whaaat? You're popular, Tama. You could start anytime.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな適当なのは嫌なのっ」
lines.english: “I don't want something that careless!”

lines.japanese: 「私の理想はね、気付いたら『なんかいいかな』って思ってる感じがいいの。それで向こうも自然と『なんかいいじゃん』みたいなことになってて」
lines.english: “My ideal is to notice that I'm thinking, ‘Maybe this is kind of nice.’ And for him to naturally be thinking, ‘Hey, this is kind of nice,’ too.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Heh.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「へへー、分かっちゃった。細川玉木の『ほほえみインサイド』って、実は単なるタマちゃんの妄想だったんだ」
lines.english: “Hee hee, I've figured it out. Tamaki Hosokawa's ‘Smile Inside’ was actually just your fantasy, Tama.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、図星ー」
lines.english: “Oh, bull's-eye.”

lines.japanese: 「……ひ、秘密だからね」
lines.english: “...I-it's a secret, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、次はどんな妄想を見せてくれるのかなあ」
lines.english: “Hee hee. What kind of fantasy will you show me next?”

lines.japanese: 「次は恋愛もの書かないもん」
lines.english: “I'm not writing a romance next.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そうなの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Really?”

lines.japanese: 「たぶん……うん、まだ迷ってるし、担当さんには止められてるんだけど」
lines.english: “Probably... Yeah, I'm still deciding, and my editor is trying to stop me.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、だって私ネットとかでよく見るけど、全国の恋に恋する少女たちが、細川先生の甘ぁ～いラブストーリーをハァハァゆって待ちのぞんでるよ？」
lines.english: “Of course. I see it online all the time. Girls in love with love all over the country are breathlessly waiting for Ms. Hosokawa's sweeeet love stories.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……それは嬉しいんだけど、逆にリアリティがなさすぎるって批判も多くて。恋愛描写がおままごとみたいだとかって」
lines.english: “Yeah... I'm happy about that, but there are also lots of people criticizing them for being too unrealistic. Saying the romance feels like playing house.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そこがいいのにー」
lines.english: “Whaaat? That's what's good about it.”

lines.japanese: 「もういいよ、なんでこんな話？　たしかリンダの恋愛話だよね」
lines.english: “Enough already. Why are we talking about this? Wasn't this about your love life?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、そっか。あれ、どこまで話したっけ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Huh, where did I get to?”

lines.japanese: 「だからええと、なんて言ったっけ、その、リンダの好きなひと。ハラダさん？」
lines.english: “So, um, what was his name? The person you like. Harada?”

lines.japanese: 「ハネダだよう！　あわわ、タマちゃん声が大きい」
lines.english: “Haneda! Oh, oh, Tama, your voice is too loud.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあＨとしよう。状況を整理すると、リンダの好きなＨには──」
lines.english: “Then let's call him H. To sum up, the H you like has—”

lines.japanese: 「呼び捨てしないで」
lines.english: “Don't call him just H.”

lines.japanese: 「Ｈさんには熱愛中の異性がいて──」
lines.english: “Mr. H has a woman he's passionately in love with—”

lines.japanese: 「熱愛ってほどじゃない」
lines.english: “Not that passionately.”

lines.japanese: 「熱愛ってほどじゃない関係の異性がいて、しかしこの女は、Ｈさんの目の届かないところで他の男と──」
lines.english: “A woman he's not that passionately involved with, but this woman, out of Mr. H's sight, with another man—”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、目は届いてた」
lines.english: “No, he could see.”

lines.japanese: 「目の届くところで他の男と浮気──」
lines.english: “In his sight, she's cheating with another man—”

lines.japanese: 「──て、うるさいリンダ。先進まない」
lines.english: “—you're noisy, Linda. We're not getting anywhere.”

lines.japanese: 「あとね？　エイチって言うと英一みたいで『誰？』って感じだから、そこはエッチって読んで。あ、もちろん呼び捨ては禁止だよ」
lines.english: “Also? When you say ‘Aitch,’ it sounds like someone's name, and I think, ‘Who?’ So make it ‘Itch.’ Oh, and remember the ‘Mr.’”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあエッチさん？　なにそれ、なんだか卑猥なひとみたいじゃない？　敬称がぜんぜん敬称になってないし、その敬い方って、おげれつ大王とかロリコン伯爵と同じラインだよね」
lines.english: “Mr. Itch? What's that? Doesn't it sound like a man with an itch he shouldn't scratch? The respectful title isn't respectful at all. That's the same sort of respect as King Filth or Count Pedophile.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、でも『エッチさん』ってほらこう、丸っこい袋文字で書くとハイ、ほのぼの４コマのタイトル風ー」
lines.english: “Whaaat? But ‘Mr. Itch,’ look, written in round bubble letters—there. Like the title of a cozy comic strip.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ほんと、夕刊っぽい。あれでしょ、主人公ニコニコ顔のおじさんで、根はいいひとなんだけどちょっとエッチなのが玉に瑕、みたいな」
lines.english: “Oh, you're right. Very evening-paper. The hero's a smiling middle-aged man, fundamentally good, but with a bit of a dirty mind as his one flaw, right?”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ違うよ、それじゃ掲載紙が駅売りスポーツ新聞だよ。エッチさんは本当はエッチじゃないんだけど、痴漢の冤罪であらぬ濡れ衣を着せられちゃっただけなの」
lines.english: “No, no. Then it'd run in one of those sports papers sold at stations. Mr. Itch isn't actually dirty-minded. He's just been falsely accused of groping someone.”

lines.japanese: 「でもそのせいで出世コースから外れて、社史編纂室に飛ばされちゃって、給湯室のＯＬたちにはＨさんなんて仇名で呼ばれて笑われる日々で、ところがＨさんの作った社内紙が伝説の先代社長の目に止まって……」
lines.english: “But that knocks him off the promotion track, and he gets transferred to the company-history office. The office women laugh at him in the kitchenette, calling him Mr. Itch. But then the company paper he makes catches the legendary former president’s eye...”

lines.japanese: 「それ、ほのぼの４コマで扱うにはテーマ重過ぎじゃない？」
lines.english: “Isn't that a bit too heavy a subject for a cozy comic strip?”

lines.japanese: 「そう？　じゃあいいよ、青年コミック誌に移るから」
lines.english: “Is it? Okay, then. I'll move it to a men's comic magazine.”

lines.japanese: 「ヤングなんとか系？　それなら読者層を考えて、やっぱり最初の設定に戻さないと。たぶん、エッチなシーンとかも多少必要になると思うし」
lines.english: “One of those ‘Young Something’ magazines? Considering the readers, you'd have to go back to the first version. They'd probably want a few racy scenes too.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうもの？」
lines.english: “That's how it works?”

lines.japanese: 「分からないけど、おそらく編集サイドは言ってくるよ」
lines.english: “I don't know, but the editors would probably ask for them.”

lines.japanese: 「そっかあ、じゃあエッチさんに恋人か奥さんを作ってあげよう。Ｈの次だからＩちゃんでいっか？」
lines.english: “Okay, then, let's give Mr. Itch a girlfriend or wife. I comes after H, so she can be Miss I.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、どうせならＪも出そう。ジェイ。名前の響き的には、ワイルドな無頼漢キャラかなあ」
lines.english: “Then while we're at it, let's add J. Jay. Going by the sound of the name, maybe a wild, rebellious type.”

lines.japanese: 「そしたらＫは？　ケイの語感的に女の子？　うーん、個人的には、女の子みたいに可愛い男の子っていうポジションが好みなんだけど……あー、あと学ラン着せたーい」
lines.english: “And K? Kay sounds like a girl's name? Hmm, personally, I'd rather make him a boy cute enough to be a girl... Oh, and I want to put him in a stand-collar school uniform.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ケイだけサラリーマンじゃないの？　うそ、じゃジェイも同じクラスでいいよ。あれ？　これ学園漫画にした方がよくない？　そうだよ、全寮制の男子校でさ、夜はバンドとかやってるの」
lines.english: “Huh? Only Kay isn't an office worker? No way. Then Jay can be in the same class. Wait, shouldn't this be a school comic? Yeah. An all-boys boarding school, and they play in a band at night.”

lines.japanese: 「いいー、それ採用ー。でもメンバー少ないね、ＬとかＭとかもっと増やさないと」
lines.english: “Nice, let's use that. But there aren't enough members. We need to add L or M or someone.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ私、落ちついた感じのキャラ欲しいな。実写化するとき細川隆二あてたい」
lines.english: “Then I'd like a calm character. I'd want Ryuuji Hosokawa to play him in the live-action version.”

lines.japanese: 「あとは、背の低いツリ目の生意気系とか？　でも人数多いと個々の出番が減っちゃうよね、どうしよう」
lines.english: “And maybe a short, sharp-eyed, bratty one? But if there are too many, each gets less time. What do we do?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと削ろうか。とりあえずもうＨとかいらないよね」
lines.english: “Shall we cut a few? We don't need H anymore, for a start.”

lines.japanese: 「だねー、ひとり世界観崩してるもんね。そもそも、なんでこの中にＨいるんだっけ」
lines.english: “Right. He ruins the whole setting all by himself. Why was H in here to begin with?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだっけ？　ああ、原田さん？」
lines.english: “Why was he? Oh, Harada?”

lines.japanese: 「誰って、だからリンダの……あ」
lines.english: “Who? I mean, your... Oh.”

lines.japanese: タマちゃんの表情が急に険しくなりました。近視なのに眼鏡やコンタクトを嫌っている彼女が、離れた点に目を凝らすときの癖です。
lines.english: Tama's expression suddenly sharpened. She's nearsighted but dislikes glasses and contacts. It's a habit when she squints at a distant point.

lines.japanese: 「会いたくない先輩がいた」
lines.english: “There's an older student I don't want to meet.”

lines.japanese: ぼそっと呟きながら、俯いて顔の上半分を手で覆いました。
lines.english: Muttering, she looked down and covered the upper half of her face with a hand.

lines.japanese: 「ふうん？」
lines.english: “Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 私はさりげなさを装って、タマちゃんの見た先を振りかえってみました。昼休み終了直前の学食には、まだほどよく利用者が残っていて、さてどの人物が彼女の忌避する対象なのやら見当がつきません。
lines.english: Pretending to be casual, I turned toward where she'd looked. Just before the end of lunch break, there were still a fair number of people in the cafeteria. I couldn't guess which one she wanted to avoid.

lines.japanese: 「どういうひと？」
lines.english: “What kind of person?”

lines.japanese: 「バイト先によく来てた厄介なお客」
lines.english: “A troublesome customer who used to come in a lot.”

lines.japanese: タマちゃんは顔を伏せたまま言いました。
lines.english: Tama spoke with her face still lowered.

lines.japanese: 「こっちは仕事中なのに、大した用もなく話しかけてくるの。ただの店員と客だってのに、やたら馴れ馴れしい口調でさあ！　せっかく会わなくなったのに、実は同じ学校だったなんて知られたくない……」
lines.english: “He'd talk to me for no real reason while I was working. We were just a waitress and a customer, but he kept acting so familiar! I'd finally stopped seeing him. I don't want him to find out we're actually at the same school...”

lines.japanese: タマちゃんは作家デビューが決まる以前まで、放課後や休日に『アレキサンダー』というお洒落なレストランでアルバイトをしていました。
lines.english: Until her debut as a writer was decided, Tama worked after school and on days off at a stylish restaurant called Alexander.

lines.japanese: 美人のタマちゃんがメイドさんみたいな可愛い服でお仕事している様子を見たくて、私も何度かお邪魔したことがあります。
lines.english: I visited a few times because I wanted to see beautiful Tama at work in a cute uniform like a maid's.

lines.japanese: たしかに、あんな可愛いウェイトレスさんだったら、ついお近付きになりたいと思っちゃったりする気持ちも分からないではありません。でも、もちろん、相手に迷惑をかけるのは駄目ですけどね。
lines.english: Certainly, I can understand wanting to get to know such a cute waitress. But of course, it's wrong to bother her.

lines.japanese: 「しかも、あとで知ったんだけど、有名なんだってあのひと、女の子には誰でも声かけまくるってことで」
lines.english: “And I found out later he's famous for it. Talking to every girl he sees.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー、日本にもいるんだねえ、そういうイタリア人みたいなひと」
lines.english: “Oh, so Japan has people like that too. Like Italians.”

lines.japanese: 「リンダ見過ぎ。窓側の女子四人座ってるテーブル、その脇に立ってる茶髪の男」
lines.english: “You’re looking around too much, Linda. The table with four girls by the window. The brown-haired guy standing beside it.”

lines.japanese: 学食中を見渡す私の上半身の旋回角度は、すでに「さりげなく」の範疇を超えていたようです。タマちゃんが警告といっしょにヒントをくれました。
lines.english: Apparently, the angle through which I'd turned my upper body to survey the cafeteria had already exceeded the bounds of ‘casual.’ Tama gave me a hint along with her warning.

lines.japanese: 窓側のテーブル……その脇に立ってる……
lines.english: The table by the window... Standing beside it...

lines.japanese: 「あっ！」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: いました。
lines.english: There he was.

lines.japanese: けれどそれは見覚えのある顔、さっきの三年生、つまりプリンセスの浮気相手そのひとだったのです。
lines.english: But it was a familiar face. The third-year from earlier. In other words, the very boy the Princess was cheating with.

lines.japanese: あわわわわ……。
lines.english: Oh, oh, oh...

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃん逃げよう」
lines.english: “Tama, let's run.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　いや、いいよ、そこまで神経質になるほどの話でも」
lines.english: “Huh? No, it's fine. It's not something to get that nervous about.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、でも私、なんだかこう、居たたまれない気持ちで……ううう」
lines.english: “Whaaat? But I feel so... I just can’t bear to stay here... Ugh...”

lines.japanese: 「べつにリンダが気にすることないのに」
lines.english: “There's no reason for you to worry about it.”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃんが良くても私は嫌なのっ」
lines.english: “Even if you're fine, I'm not!”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　なんで？　リンダ関係ないでしょ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Why? This has nothing to do with you, does it?”

lines.japanese: 「関係ないって何ー、もう！　ひどいよタマちゃん、ひと事だと思ってー」
lines.english: “What do you mean, nothing to do with me? Honestly! You're being cruel, Tama. Acting like it's someone else's problem.”

lines.japanese: 「思ってない思ってない。や、そんなことより、リンダ声大きいから──」
lines.english: “I'm not, I'm not. Actually, more importantly, you're being loud, Linda—”

lines.japanese: 「──ってホラこっち見てるっ」
lines.english: “—see? He's looking this way!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、笑ってるし」
lines.english: “See, he's smiling.”
“Huh, huh, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ほらぁ、こっち来るー」
lines.english: “See? He's coming over!”

lines.japanese: 「う、うあ、うああああ！」
lines.english: “Ugh, aah, aaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「え……！？　ちょっ、リンダどこ行くの！」
lines.english: “Huh...?! Hey, Linda, where are you going?!”
